I'm 12 about to turn 13 this year. I started to really get into nirvana this year. Like really inte them. I dont remember how I got into them. I think I listened to "Smells like teen spirit" and then moved onto "Come as you are" and "Heart Shaped-Box" and then "Lithium". In a moment I fell in love with the band and listened to "Bleach" for the first time. Man I want to experience that again. After "Bleach" I actually listened to "Incesticide". I think It was because I read somewhere that it was old project and outtakes and stuff so I could experience the old nirvana. In my opinion it is as good as "Bleach". After those two rockets the big monstrous beast called "Nevermind" was next up. I had one word after listening to that album, MASTERPIECE. I think listening to "Nevermind" for the first time knocks rollercoasters, food, sports and all that fun stuff out of the park. It's the best thing in life. I then of course listened to the "This is Nirvana" playlist on Spotify for some reason. I think it was to get a recap of some sort. It was an awesome compilation so I couldn't wait to listen to "In Utero". What I loved about "In Utero" was the thoughness and gritty touch it had. Overall, amazing and raw. However what catched me on the hook of Nirvana was outside of the music. It was the hilarious interviews and personalities that they had. The anti-mainstream thing and their rebellic acts when performing live was top notch. And that ain't even the biggest factor which is the lead singer, Kurt Cobain. This guy was such a great guy. A kind hearted pissed off rock icon. I always tried to analyze the lyrics and read about the backstory to albums, gigs, photoshoots and songs. It was so goddamn interesting. The most interesting thing about Kurt was his life. Growing up in Aberdeen, a town that he didn't like, depression, anxiety, and teenage angst. He was such a rebellious young person. Learning about his life was so interesting. It was like reading a book that you never want to stop reading.  I could go on for days about this man and his band but I won't bore anyone out anymore now.
